page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network interfaces with a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-core capabilities alongside limited single-core execution speeds. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier, while single-threaded gzip compression is in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including Passmark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, consistently register in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the overall Passmark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

This resource allocation profile makes the instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but do not require high single-threaded compute performance. Examples include database operations, Redis caching layers, and static web serving, all of which achieved average tier performance in benchmark testing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense memory footprint relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound applications where raw CPU clock speed is not the primary bottleneck.
